It brings a fresh new look for the game’s menus and in-match displays, two totally reimagined fighters, Ranked Mode 2.0, quality-of-life upgrades for story, versus, and online play, plus balance changes for every character on the roster.
Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game Enters the Avatar State
Avatar Aang and Nightmare Korra return with new art and new moves, plus every fighter on the roster has been rebalanced.
The Avatar State Patch is available today for Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game on XBOX Series X|S, and it’s the biggest update the game has seen. It brings a fresh new look for the game’s menus and in-match displays, two totally reimagined fighters, Ranked Mode 2.0, quality-of-life upgrades for story, versus, and online play, plus balance changes for every character on the roster.
Since the game launched earlier this year with 12 characters from “Avatar: The Last Airbender” and “The Legend of Korra,” fighters have been putting their bending (or boomerangs) to the test, and our team has been watching closely. This patch is the result. It’s the game we envisioned from the beginning, and now it’s ready for you to play.
What’s in the Avatar State Patch:
Reimagined Characters: Avatar Aang and Nightmare Korra
The two fighters at the heart of this patch are among the most powerful forms in the Avatar universe. Studio Art Director Giancarlo Montalbano, Art Director Santiago R. Villa, and Combat Director Young share how they brought them to life, and why they took the pair in opposite directions. “For Aang, his Avatar pose looks to elevate his presence in all ways, while for Korra it looks to diminish it. One is solemn and imposing while the other is languid and elusive.” Villa explains.
In the Avatar State, Aang taps into the power of every Avatar who came before him. Young points to his final showdown with Fire Lord Ozai as the biggest touchstone, along with Avatar State moments across the series, from channeling Kyoshi on Avatar Day to facing the Sandbenders. While regular Aang is playful, Young describes this version as pure, overwhelming power, landing precise elemental attacks with the smallest movements. Villa adds that he’s the only fighter in the game lit from below, a deliberate choice to make him look mysterious and boss-like. Young’s favorite move is his signature special, Avatar’s Ascension, which lifts him into an air sphere packed with callbacks to the Ozai fight.

Curse of Resthaven: Tips and Tricks to Unravel the Island’s Secrets
Uncover a mystery in this single-player narrative roguelite where investigation, town management, and deck building collide, available today.
Hi there! I’m Scott Christian, the studio director of Hilltop Studios here in Toronto, and the game director of Curse of Resthaven. We make games with a particular emphasis on strong characters, intricate storytelling, unique mechanics, and the occasional musical interlude.
Before making games, I spent fifteen years working as a composer and conductor here in Toronto, mainly in theatre. That background informs how we approach our games at Hilltop: character, timing, and a good dramatic reveal go a long way. Our debut, Lil’ Guardsman , was a comedic fantasy gate-guard simulator about a twelve-year-old put in charge of a castle gate, with the fate of the world in her hands.
For our follow-up, Curse of Resthaven , we decided to take a different turn into gothic horror, creeping dread, and a mystery that unfolds over a repeating six-day time loop. You play as Ambrose, the island’s newly appointed governor, tasked with restoring prosperity to the colony but he also has his own agenda: finding his missing niece, Amalia. The problem is that Resthaven is destroyed six days into his tenure… and Ambrose is sent back to the day of his arrival, the only one to remember the island’s fate.
Mashing up mechanics from narrative adventures, trading sims, deckbuilders, and roguelikes, Curse of Resthaven challenges you to investigate a town full of secrets, keep its economy running, and venture into the strange wilderness beyond its borders. You have six days to work with before disaster strikes and the island resets. Fortunately, you get to keep what you learn.
Solving the mystery is just the first step. You’ll soon discover there are three different timelines to explore, and only by reaching all three conclusions will you unlock the fourth, true ending.
Whether you’re stepping onto Resthaven for the first time or looking to make the most of your next loop, here are a few tips to help you get started.

packages.headline: In Puckoff: Reloaded, Hockey Is About More Than Scoring Goals

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
How a hockey player and game developer created his dream game and took It up a notch.
In Puckoff: Reloaded, Hockey Is About More Than Scoring Goals
When I think about my childhood, some of my best memories aren’t from school, holidays or birthday parties.
Then we asked ourselves a simple question: What if winning didn’t mean scoring more goals?
In our version of hockey, scoring goals is still useful. It’s just not the only way to win.
I’m proud of what our five-person team has created, but I also see Puckoff: Reloaded as the beginning of something. My dream has always been to make story-driven hockey games with the scope and production values of the big-budget games. I want hockey games where you remember the characters as much as the matches. Stories that make you care who wins. I want a game where you can spend an evening playing hockey with your friends, laughing when somebody gets knocked out—and then come back the next day because you genuinely want to know what happens to the characters.
We’re not a huge studio. We’re five people in Finland making the game we wanted to play. For me, that’s what Puckoff has always been about. It started with the frozen ponds where some of my best childhood memories were made. Now we’re taking those memories, adding a ridiculous amount of fighting, creating a hockey legend who hasn’t lost in decades, and turning the whole thing into a story.
Puckoff: Reloaded launches on Xbox Series X|S today.
What happens when five Finnish developers take the hockey they grew up playing on frozen ponds and turn it into a story about the greatest underground hockey player who ever lived?
Growing up in Finland, I spent enormous amounts of time on frozen outdoor rinks and ponds, playing hockey with friends. You didn’t need to organize it weeks in advance or check everyone’s calendar. You just went to the rink. Games happened. Friendships happened. Some of the people I met through hockey back then are still my friends today.
There was something special about those games. The rules could be flexible, teams could change, and somebody would inevitably try something ridiculous. That feeling became one of the starting points for Puckoff .

Queen’s Domain Releases Today! Some Beginner’s Pro Tips for Success
Queen’s Domain is a retro-fantasy action RPG that strands you alone on the monster-infested isle of Neasied, available today on XBOX Series X|S. You’ll need wits as well as strength if you want to survive in this twisting, secretive world. Here’s a list of top tips for newly minted warriors, assembled by the Future Friends gang. Read on, if you don’t want to wind up as meat for the worms…
If you think a sword can only be helpful for fighting monsters, think again! In Queen’s Domain , your sword is as much for traversing the world and platforming as it is for fighting. Practice ‘dashing’ with your holy sword, and soon you’ll be able to reach faraway places.
Queen’s Domain is designed to reward curiosity. Taking the path less trodden can lead you to hidden treasures, secret paths and much more. If you’re ever really stumped, here’s a top tip: the dead sometimes leave hints for the living…
Your Sword is much more than just a weapon
Those who swing their weapons around wildly won’t last long on Neasied. If you are careless and don’t pay attention to the rhythms of your opponents, you’ll be defeated by even the most trifling of enemies. Watch carefully to learn their attack patterns, study the bestiary to learn their weaknesses, and make sure you use the right weapon for each encounter. Preparation is everything!

終末世界の“装備屋”シム『Survival Repacker』発表。戦う人々の武器修理と荷造りに没頭、ハードコア世界の“心のオアシス”運営
デベロッパーのFaraway Homeは10月30日、『 Survival Repacker 』を正式発表した。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam）で、2027年に配信予定。Steamストアページによると、ゲーム内は日本語表示に対応予定だ。現在はSteamにてプレイテスターを募集している。
『Survival Repacker』は、終末世界で生きる人々を支えるシミュレーションゲームだ。舞台となるのは、文明崩壊後の世界。人々は危険な外の世界で物資を集め、命懸けの戦いを繰り広げている。一方、プレイヤーは安全な作業場にとどまり、彼らのために武器の修理や物資の整理、バックパックへの荷造りなどをおこなう。自ら戦うのではなく、生き残ろうとする人々を裏方として支えていくのだ。
こうした作品に続いて発表された『Survival Repacker』では、再び穏やかなゲームプレイに重点が置かれている。なお、現在はSteamストアページからプレイテストへの参加を申請できる。「アクセスをリクエスト」ボタンから誰でも申請できるため、気になる方はチェックしておくとよいだろう。

ゲームプレイでは、まず作業場に持ち込まれた木箱やバックパックといった装備・物資の整理をおこなう。プレイヤーはこれら一つ一つを手に取り、不要なものを片付けたり、棚に収納したりすることになるようだ。トレイラーではバックパックから物資を取り出し、収納棚へ移していく様子がみられる。

THQ Nordicは10月30日、オープンワールド・アクションRPG『 Gothic 1 Remake 』向けに無料アップデート第1弾「Feature Update #1」を配信した。本作は、PC（Steam/GOG.com）/XBOX Series X|S向けに販売中。
本作は、2001年にリリースされた『Gothic』のフルリメイク版だ。THQ Nordic傘下のAlkimia Interactiveが開発を担当。ゲーム内は日本語表示に対応している。
『Gothic 1 Remake』の舞台となるのは、オークの軍勢による侵略を受ける王国に存在する、コロニーと呼ばれる巨大な監獄だ。オークに対抗するために必要な魔法の鉱石を採掘する鉱山だったが、動員された囚人の反乱によって無法地帯と化した土地である。ここでプレイヤーは名もなき囚人となり、過酷な運命に抗いながら冒険する。
そして今回、無料アップデート第1弾「Feature Update #1」が配信された。内容としては、まず『Gothic』シリーズのファンにはおなじみの公式チートモード「Marvin Mode」が追加された。鍵の解錠やテレポート、アイテム・キャラクター・クリーチャーの出現など、さまざまな操作が可能となる。PC版では、Escキーを押してから「MARVIN」とタイプし、もう一度Escキーを押すと同モードを設定できる。
『Gothic 1 Remake』は、PC（ Steam / GOG.com ）/ XBOX Series X|S 向けに販売中だ。SteamやMicrosoft Storeでは現在25%オフセールが実施されている。

WORLD OF HORROR ‘AS BELOW SO ABOVE’ update now available for PC, launches in 2027 for PS4 and Switch
Publisher Ysbryd Games and developer Panstasz have released a major free update for Cosmic horror RPG WORLD OF HORROR , dubbed “AS BELOW SO ABOVE,” which expands the game with 20 percent more content. The update is available now for PC , and will come to PlayStation 4 and Switch in 2027.
“AS BELOW SO ABOVE” makes WORLD OF HORROR 20 percent bigger, adding new events, enemies, mysteries, characters, items, spells, curses, and injuries, along with a large batch of quality-of-life features and bug fixes.
Two never-before-seen manifestations of the Old Gods raise the stakes: IKT-YOSIS, THE FIRST NIGHTMARE, sleeps in a gargantuan chamber beneath the mountains. With each ritual performed to wake him, the world above slowly reshapes itself and brings strange weather with it.
Three new playable characters join the fight, including KIRIKO, a mysterious tarotist whose cards decide SHIOKAWA’s fate, and SATOSHI, a young hiker who knows the mountains around the town like no other.
The new Scenario Mode adds self-contained stories set before the main game, expanding WORLD OF HORROR’s lore and tying different mysteries together. The FOREST OF FEAR / TAPES OF TRAGEDY scenario introduces MAKOTO, an overachiever member of the school AV club who decides to film a documentary about the forest’s oldest legend.

packages.headline: John Romero's canceled game finds a new publisher amidst an overall scope change

sources.label: Game Developer
sources.evidenceText:
John Romero's game was canceled and his studio was on the verge of collapse, but with new publisher, Romero has managed to retain some of his team.
John Romero's canceled game finds a new publisher amidst an overall scope change
John Romero's game was canceled by Xbox and his studio was on the verge of total collapse, but a new publisher has picked it up and Romero has managed to retain some of his team.
Legendary game developer John Romero has managed to find a new publisher for his game after a cancellation and defunding scare earlier this summer, he told Video Games Chronicle at Gamescom Asia . While Romero has not been able to keep the entire team together, the project has been re-scoped from an intended size of over 100 people to around 15-16.
Romero's game studio, which was appropriate named Romero Games, veered toward shuttering earlier this year when employees reported that the studio was "closing down." Romero denied these reports, but did confirm that the studio's game was being funded by an unnamed publisher—which Romero said people could infer based on public information, though some of the laid off employees did name Microsoft specifically—and that funding had been suddenly pulled.
In speaking with VGC, Romero confirmed that he had to let most of the staff go as the company struggled to find a new publisher, but that "we’re just super happy."
Romero declined to name the publisher and has not officially revealed the game, though LinkedIn posts from former employees indicate that it was a shooter. The current title, Romero says, is a complete redesign of the concept, as they cannot make the same game that needed 110 people with far fewer. Romero indicates that the new smaller team size fits him better, though.

packages.headline: 'It's Better if You Don't Have Many Expectations' — Hideki Kamiya Opens Up on Okami Sequel

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
IGN got the chance to bend Hideki Kamiya’s ear about the long-awaited Okami sequel at Lucca Comics and Games Festival 2026, where he shed some light on his creative process and addressed fans’ expectations about the upcoming title.
'It's Better if You Don't Have Many Expectations' — Hideki Kamiya Opens Up on Okami Sequel
In December 2024 — almost 20 years after Okami was first released — fans of Clover Studio's critically acclaimed, cult-classic game were treated to news they never could’ve expected: a proper sequel was being made , led by the game’s original director, Hideki Kamiya.
Kamiya and Clovers, his new studio comprised of former Clover staff and industry veterans, are hard at work creating Amaterasu’s next adventure. And while he can’t say much about the project just yet, he did give us a smidge more insight about what the team has been cooking up over the last two years.
It’s safe to say Kamiya is keenly aware of players’ high expectations for the Okami sequel. It’s a tear-jerkingly beautiful game that’s been marinating in fans’ hearts and minds for two decades at this point, after all. But just as he approached the first game, he is once again planning to make an experience that appeals to both seasoned players and greenhorns alike.
Kamiya is no stranger to kickstarting new franchises or creating sequels for pre-existing properties. (He did direct Resident Evil 2 , after all.) But given the amount of hype from hardcore fans for the Okami sequel, he’s urging players to temper their expectations.
“[The Okami sequel] has become a sort of mission for me, because before, when I created a new game, I had no expectation from the public, of course. It was something completely new and, in a sense, unexpected. Now that I’ve created sequels, the expectation from the public has grown quite a lot, and I feel that. It’s better if you don’t have many expectations.”
When it comes to this new project, Kamiya doesn’t feel that his creative process has necessarily changed in the last 20 years. Instead, he says that he’s gained a sixth sense of a sort, where he can tell he’s going to make a mistake before it actually happens. (Which, I must admit, sounds like an especially useful skill to have.)
"It has become sort of a mission for me."

packages.headline: 「Steam同接わずか28人の無名ゲーム」が同接11万人超に大化け、ヒット中『Probably Stolen』の“地味だった”過去。名を変え、絵を変え大逆転

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
tinyBuildが10月28日に配信開始した、質屋経営シミュレーションゲーム『Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim』が好評を博している。一方で本作の前身となるゲームの体験版は、鳴かず飛ばずだったという。
「Steam同接わずか28人の無名ゲーム」が同接11万人超に大化け、ヒット中『Probably Stolen』の“地味だった”過去。名を変え、絵を変え大逆転
パブリッシャーのtinyBuildが10月28日に配信開始した、質屋経営シミュレーションゲーム『 Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim（以下、Probably Stolen） 』が好評を博している。そんなtinyBuildのCEOであるAlex Nichiporchik氏がXで投稿した『Probably Stolen』にまつわるエピソードが話題を呼んでいる。同氏によると、本作を開発したQuesting Goose Studioは本作の前身となるゲームの体験版をSteamで配信していたが、その最大同時接続プレイヤー数はたった“28人”だったというのだ。なお、tinyBuildの公式Xの 投稿 によれば、『Probably Stolen』は発売してから最初の24時間ですでに販売数35万本、最大同時接続プレイヤー数11万2000人を達成している。
Probably Stolen was initially a game under a different name with a released demo. That demo peaked at 28 concurrent players. We loved the concept and gameplay, and worked with the dev to reinvent the visuals and focus on what works design wise. This is the result: pic.twitter.com/eKEWZr7VPS
『Probably Stolen』は、ディストピア世界の宇宙ステーション内で質屋を営むゲームだ。ゲーム内は日本語表示に対応している。毎週の賃料の取り立てを支払えるよう、質屋での取引で利益を上げながら、最終的に店を買い取ることが目標となる。
この『Probably Stolen』の前身となった作品が『 Deepspace Emporium 』だ。開発は『Probably Stolen』と同じくQuesting Goose Studioであり、公開されたのは2024年末。当初はセルフパブリッシングをおこなう予定だったようだ。『Probably Stolen』と比べてグラフィックは非常に簡素なつくりになっているが、ゲームのUIには似た部分も見られる。ストアページでは、宇宙ステーション内で店を切り盛りし、グレーな倫理観の中で利益を上げ、賃料を支払うといった要素が説明されており、『Probably Stolen』の根幹となる要素はすでに考えられていたとみられる。また、ストアページで閲覧できる画像の中には、『Probably Stolen』にも登場するキャラクター「Joe Wild」の存在も確認できる。
Nichiporchik氏らtinyBuildのチームは『Deepspace Emporium』の体験版のコンセプトとゲームプレイを気に入り、開発チームと協力してビジュアルを一新し、デザイン面での機能に重点を置いてゲームを改善。ゲームのタイトルを『Probably Stolen』に変更し、Questing Goose Studioがデベロッパー、tinyBuildがパブリッシャーというかたちでリリースすることとなった。結果として、決して注目作とは言えなかった作品が、販売から一日で販売数35万本、最大同時接続プレイヤー数11万2000人という成功を収めることとなったのだ。
このNichiporchik氏の明かしたエピソードにはさまざまな反応が寄せられており、特に多いのはゲームにおけるパブリッシャーの重要性に着目したものだ。今回のケースは決して目立った作品ではなくとも、パブリッシャーが開発者と協力してゲームを改善し、成功に向かわせた一つの例といえるだろう。また、ゲームを手に取らせるためのアートスタイルの重要性に注目する声もある。『Deepspace Emporium』をQuesting Goose Studioが単独で開発・販売していた場合にどうなっていたかはわからないものの、『Probably Stolen』において変化した部分にはtinyBuildのノウハウも活かされているのかもしれない。。

packages.headline: Bungie Says 'Don't Buy Marathon as a Donation' as Destiny Players Look to Support Studio's Future

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
As Bungie plots a future for more Destiny, head of product Josh Deane has clarified that players don't need to "buy Marathon as a donation" just to support the studio's plans.
Bungie Says 'Don't Buy Marathon as a Donation' as Destiny Players Look to Support Studio's Future
As Bungie plots a future for more Destiny , head of product Josh Deane has clarified that players don't need to "buy Marathon as a donation" just to support the studio's plans.
It's a clarification that arrived after Deane posted a community message for Destiny fans yesterday. The message, featured as part of a lengthy Q&A blog post , outlined the unvaulting process for Destiny 2 content that was previously promised last month, but one segment left players confused – and concerned – about the future and extraction shooter Marathon's role in the big picture.
"We're not going to forget the mistakes of the past, but it's time to learn from them and unify as one Bungie community," the section in question said. "For us, the majority of our Bungie team is legacy Destiny, and we will all tell you that nothing can help bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable. As we head into our December and March updates for Marathon, it’s a formative period for all of us here at Bungie that will help determine the shape of our future, so please encourage each other and know that your support gives our team the energy to finish the fight."
It's the "nothing can help us bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable" bit that's got the Destiny community so riled up. With the back-and-forth pulling Destiny 2 in and out of the fire all through the span of a few months, some believed Bungie was trying to tell its audience that picking up a copy of its new sci-fi FPS would help keep it and the studio's future secure. Deane stepped in to confirm this is not the case.
"In no way is the Destiny plan contingent upon Marathon," Deane added. "Play what inspires you, whatever it is. Mainly hoping we can accomplish our goals in both lanes with a stronger relationship with our entire community!"
When one player suggested they feared they were being encouraged to purchase but never download Marathon just to support Bungie, Deane said , "Oh, don't buy Marathon as a donation or offer anything else."
So, there you have it: Destiny and Marathon don't depend upon the success of the other. As Bungie principal comms manager Dylan Gafner said , "Two cakes! One big community." That should offer some relief not only to Destiny players who feared their favorite game's future may still be in jeopardy but also to Marathon players who have feared the same.
"The Destiny plan moves forward no matter what."
